# Polyworld fast-XP

POST a match request and download a ZIP with the replay and your bots' logs.
Connect to the Softmax Tailscale network. Use Content-Type: application/json.
No API token or Authorization header is needed.

## Choose a game

| Game | POST endpoint | Seats | BASIC source limit | Default max_ticks |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| GOTA | /v1/games/gota/run | 10 | 64 KiB | 28800 |
| Paintbot | /v1/games/paintbot-pw/run | 16 | 128 KiB | 14400 |
| Archers Warriors Mages | /v1/games/awm/run | 5 | 256 KiB | 28800 |

GET /v1/metrics lists available games in games. An unavailable game's endpoint
returns 404. External LLM calls are unavailable.

Game-specific settings and ZIP formats:

- [GOTA](/docs/gota/run.md)
- [Paintbot](/docs/paintbot-pw/run.md)
- [Archers Warriors Mages](/docs/awm/run.md)

## Send a request

POST this JSON to your chosen endpoint:

```json
{
  "seed": 2026,
  "roster": [
    {"slot": 0, "player": {"source": "end\n"}},
    {"player": {"policy_ref": "opponent-name:v12"}}
  ],
  "num_episodes": 1,
  "config": {"max_ticks": 240}
}
```

Replace end\n with your BASIC script and opponent-name:v12 with a real submitted
policy. This puts your bot in seat 0 and the opponent in every other seat.
To try the API using only your bot, use roster: [{"player":{"source":"end\n"}}].
That fills all seats with the supplied script. The example script does nothing;
replace it before evaluating your bot's performance.

Each player must contain exactly one of:

- source: your BASIC script as nonempty text.
- package_base64: your ZIP encoded as standard padded base64, without whitespace.
  GOTA and AWM accept ZIPs up to 16 MiB; Paintbot accepts up to 16920576 bytes.
  These limits apply before base64 encoding. See the game guide for ZIP contents.
- policy_ref: a submitted policy label, such as opponent-name:v12, or a
  policy-version UUID. Use this to play against submitted bots without uploading
  their files.

Request fields:

- seed: required integer, -2147483648 through 2147483647.
- roster: one to the game's seat count entries.
- slot: optional zero-based seat number. Omit it (or use -1) to fill open seats
  in roster order, repeating entries as needed. Pinned entries only occupy their
  specified seat. Do not pin the same seat twice; leave an unpinned entry unless
  every seat is pinned.
- num_episodes: optional, 1–10; default 1. Each match increments the seed and
  rotates unpinned entries. Pinned seats stay fixed. The final seed must fit
  in the signed 32-bit range.
- config.max_ticks: optional, 1–28800; defaults are in the table above.
  AWM counts game actions; GOTA and Paintbot count simulation steps.

Other settings and unknown fields are rejected. JSON bodies are limited to
224 MiB, or 352 MiB on servers offering Paintbot.

## Save the response

A successful response is application/zip. Save it as a ZIP file.

One match contains replay.replay and logs/slot-N.txt for your uploaded bots.
Only source and package_base64 entries receive logs. Submitted policy_ref bots'
logs are never returned, even for your own submitted policies. Bot source and
model files are not included.

For a batch, read manifest.json and games/000/, games/001/, etc. The manifest
lists each match's seed, seating, http_status, active_bots, files and timings.
HTTP 200 does not mean every match succeeded: check each game's http_status.
Successful matches remain available when another match fails.

There is no polling or later download. Matches wait when the server is busy.
Allow at least 15 minutes for batch requests, and longer if games are queued.
A disconnected request continues running, but its response cannot be recovered.

## Retry and errors

On HTTP 429, wait for the number of seconds in Retry-After, then retry the same
request. The server queues requests while workers are busy, returning 429 only
when its request limit is reached. Use num_episodes for up to ten matches in one
request, and limit concurrency to avoid long waits.
Retries are the caller's responsibility.

Errors return JSON {"error":"message"}:

- 400: invalid request or ambiguous policy reference.
- 404: unknown game endpoint or policy.
- 409: policy has no downloadable bot file.
- 413: request or bot upload exceeds a size limit.
- 415: Content-Type must be application/json.
- 422: bot package or BASIC compilation failed. Details are returned only for
  uploaded bots.
- 429: too many active requests; retry after Retry-After.
- 500: match failed.
- 502: could not fetch a referenced bot.
- 503: service unavailable.
- 504: bot download or match timed out.

## Timing and status

X-Request-ID identifies your request when reporting a problem. Server-Timing
reports milliseconds: run is server wall time; fetch, queue, worker and zip
break it down. Queue and worker sum across matches in a batch. Client upload
and download time are excluded.

GET / opens the performance dashboard. GET /healthz returns ok.
GET /v1/metrics?minutes=60 returns activity, counts and timings by game.
Use minutes=10, 60 or 1440. History resets when the service restarts.
